messages:
sara-peopleops: Hey folks 1 1 - quick one: Omar is converting from W-2 contractor to full-time on 6/15. Do any of his contractor pay periods count toward 401(k) eligibility or employer match retroactively?
omar-eng: I asked because I missed the initial enrollment window earlier this year when I was contractor. Hope there's a path to get match for prior months.
kate-finance: Short answer: contractor earnings generally do not count toward the company 401(k) plan. Eligibility and match are tied to payroll records for employees. However, there are a couple of edge cases we should check (e.g., if he was paid through our payroll system as a temporary employee vs. 1099).
benefits@redwood: Confirming: 1099 contractor pay is not eligible for 401(k). If any payments were processed on our payroll (W-2), they could count, but we'd need payroll records. Also enrollment windows matter 1 - most plans allow new hires to enroll on conversion effective date and employer match starts with payroll cycles after enrollment.
onboarding-bot: Reminder: new-hire enrollment for omar-eng is open until 7 days after 6/15. Link: https://people.redwood.com/onboard/enroll :package:
sara-peopleops: If payroll did process some checks as W-2 temp earlier in the year, can finance/benefits do retroactive match for those paychecks?
kate-finance: If payroll shows W-2 earnings that were eligible but employee missed enrollment, vendor rules apply. Some recordkeepers accept retroactive salary deferral elections if filed within plan deadlines; retroactive employer match is rare but vendor can manual-post if plan document allows and finances approves. We'll need to open a case with the recordkeeper.
benefits@redwood: Action: kate-finance will check payroll classification for Omar and open vendor case. If payroll shows W-2 eligible earnings, vendor may allow a "catch-up deferral" election for the year (subject to IRS limits) but the match depends on plan sponsor approval.
kate-finance: Opening case now: RK-2026-2104. Asked vendor whether they accept retroactive employee deferral elections and whether they can post employer match retroactively when earnings were already paid as W-2.
omar-eng: If retroactive match is impossible, is there a one-time discretionary company contribution option so I'm not penalized for the contractor timing?
kate-finance: The company can approve a one-time discretionary contribution in some cases, but it must be processed as a separate employer contribution (not a match) and comply with nondiscrimination testing. That requires approval from payroll + finance + benefits and may be taxable in a different way. We'll coordinate if needed.
benefits@redwood: Vendor response (2026-03-02): recordkeeper accepts retroactive deferral elections for eligible W-2 pay if filed within plan-specified timelines, but they will not automatically post employer match retroactively. Manual match postings are possible only when plan sponsor (Redwood) approves and provides supporting docs. Recommended path: 1) confirm payroll W-2 earnings; 2) employee submits retroactive deferral election form to vendor; 3) finance approves any manual employer posting and funds it on next payroll cycle. Timeline: vendor turnaround 5-7 business days.
sara-peopleops: Great, thanks. Omar: please confirm if any early paychecks were W-2. If not, enroll on 6/15 and we can discuss discretionary option if leadership approves.
omar-eng: Got it -- payroll says all prior pay was 1099. I'll enroll on 6/15. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
